"This value specifies how much extra physical memory the Linux kernel keeps free. When memory runs low, the kernel immediately starts compressing memory into SWAP/ZRAM, and the device becomes noticeably slow until available memory recovers to a reasonable range.
Simply put, the larger extra_free_kbytes is, the more aggressively memory is reclaimed (swapping or killing processes). However, setting it too large is not recommended, as it wastes physical memory and increases the load on the disk/processor!"

"L1 data-cache miss count. The right-hand MISS(%) is misses as a share of accesses. Lower counts and lower ratios are better."
L1 data-cache access count. A high value only means frequent reads/writes in this period; compare it with cache-misses to judge quality.
Data memory access count (including cache hits). Shows how busy the memory subsystem is; higher values consume more bandwidth.
Pipeline stall cycles when the front end or back end cannot issue instructions. The core is waiting instead of computing; lower is better.
Back-end stall cycles. Execute/writeback cannot take new instructions, often because the core is compute-bound or waiting on memory. Lower is better.
Back-end stall cycles that are memory-bound (L1D, outer memory, TLB and stores). A high value means the bottleneck is the memory subsystem. Lower is better.
Front-end stall cycles. Fetch/decode cannot supply instructions, often due to instruction-cache misses or branch mispredicts. Lower is better.
Front-end stall cycles that are memory-bound (L1I, outer cache/memory, TLB). A high value means the bottleneck is instruction supply from the memory side. Lower is better.

In ADB mode, in addition to accessing more information‑viewing features in Scene, additional functions such as system app uninstallation and permission management will also be unlocked. If you accidentally uninstall critical system apps, you may need to perform a factory reset to be able to boot your device again. If you accept these risks, please use it with extreme caution. Carefully read all function prompts and warnings, and do not uninstall system programs of unknown purpose without careful consideration! *Scene may collect your device model, manufacturer, hardware configuration parameters, performance statistics, thermal control settings, and other data for user group analysis and to improve compatibility and adaptation.
I understand and accept the agreement

* Scene may collect your device model, manufacturer, hardware configuration parameters, performance statistics, thermal control settings and other data, and send them to the cloud for user group analysis and improved compatibility and adaptation.

When running in ROOT mode, all features of Scene become accessible, including some functions that carry certain risks. Examples include: uninstalling pre-installed system apps, controlling processor performance, and writing or restoring system files. Improper operation or functional defects during use may prevent you from accessing the system interface or result in the loss of important data. "The value ranges from 0 to 1000, where 1000 means 10%, i.e. each of the memory watermark values low/min/high differs from the next by 10% (of the physical RAM capacity).
For example (my phone): pageSize=4KB managed=1951743(pages) min_free_kbytes=10900(KB) watermark_scale_factor=500
In this case the min value is 10900(KB)/4(PageSize)=2725(pages) the low value is about 1951743*5%+2725≈100312(pages) the high value is about 1951743*10%+2725≈197899(pages) Note: the final low and high values may be larger due to extra_free_kbytes.
In this example, min=2725=10MB low=100312≈392MB high=197899≈773MB
This means memory reclaim starts when free memory drops below 392MB, and continues until available memory rises above 773MB~"
